blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Resolving conflict in a British office begins with cooling the temperature. Almost nothing is fixed while two people are still angry. The first move of a good manager is to acknowledge the issue calmly, create a little space — a coffee, a walk, a quiet room — and then bring the conversation back to the work, not the people.

Language matters here. Instead of "why did you do X?", the British way is "I wondered if we could talk through what happened with X?" Instead of "you were wrong", try "I think we may have seen this slightly differently — can I share my view?"

It sounds slow, but it is fast. By the end of a calm, well-framed twenty minutes, most British conflicts resolve quietly — and leave no bitterness behind.

items.q: According to the text, what is a good manager's first move in a conflict?
options: To acknowledge the issue calmly and create some space
To bring the two people together immediately
To ask why the mistake happened
items.why: "The first move… is to acknowledge the issue calmly, create a little space."

items.q: Why does the text say almost nothing is fixed while two people are still angry?
options: Because anger blocks a useful conversation until it cools
Because British offices avoid all disagreement
Because the work is not important
items.why: "Almost nothing is fixed while two people are still angry" — por isso se esfria a temperatura primeiro.

items.q: Once the temperature has cooled, where should the conversation be brought back to?
options: To the work, not the people
items.why: "bring the conversation back to the work, not the people."

items.q: The author suggests that reflective phrasing like "I wondered if we could talk through X?" is used because…
options: it is more formal and impressive
it lowers defensiveness and keeps the door open
it lets the manager avoid the conversation
items.why: Inferência: o contraste com "why did you do X?" mostra que a forma reflexiva suaviza e evita defensividade.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Leaving no bitterness behind is part of a good resolution
The way you phrase a message changes how it lands
Telling someone directly "you were wrong" is the quickest fix
A calm approach can actually be faster than a blunt one
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende justamente o oposto — "It sounds slow, but it is fast" e substituir "you were wrong".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie mediando um conflito entre dois colegas do time de projeto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for coming in, both of you. I know things got a bit heated after the review yesterday, so I thought a quiet room and a coffee might help more than another email thread.

Before we get into anything, I want to say I'm not here to decide who was right. That's genuinely not the point. What I'd like is for us to talk through what actually happened on the timeline, because I think we may have seen the same situation slightly differently — and that's fine.

Daniel, I wondered if we could start with what you needed from the data team last week. Not what went wrong — just what you were expecting. And then, Priya, I'd love to hear how it looked from your side, because I suspect the brief reached you in a different shape.

My honest guess is that nobody dropped the ball here. The handover was rushed, the deadline moved twice, and two careful people ended up frustrated with each other over a process problem. So let's keep this about the work. Twenty calm minutes now, and I think we walk out of here with no hard feelings — and a cleaner handover next time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why did Sophie choose a quiet room and a coffee for the meeting?
options: Because it helps more than another email thread after things got heated
Because she wanted the conversation to be formal
Because it was the only room available
Because coffee is a company tradition
items.why: "a quiet room and a coffee might help more than another email thread."

items.q: What does Sophie say she is NOT there to do?
options: To improve the handover next time
items.why: "I'm not here to decide who was right. That's genuinely not the point."

items.q: How does Sophie ask Daniel to begin?
options: By describing what he was expecting from the data team
items.why: "what you needed… Not what went wrong — just what you were expecting."

items.q: What does Sophie suggest was the real cause of the conflict?
options: A lack of experience on the team
A process problem — a rushed handover and a moving deadline
A personality clash between two difficult people
items.why: Inferência: "nobody dropped the ball… a process problem" — ela desloca a culpa das pessoas para o processo.

items.q: What outcome does Sophie expect from the twenty-minute conversation?
options: A longer meeting scheduled for later
A decision on who to blame
No hard feelings and a cleaner handover next time
items.why: "we walk out of here with no hard feelings — and a cleaner handover next time."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The first thing she did was cool the temperature in the room." This means she…
options: reduced the tension between the people
raised her voice to take control
items.why: Cool the temperature = esfriar/baixar a tensão emocional entre as pessoas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A good mediator will ___ the issue calmly before trying to solve it."
items.why: Acknowledge = reconhecer; reconhecer a questão com calma antes de resolvê-la.

items.q: "The goal is to leave no bitterness behind." Bitterness is…
items.why: Bitterness = amargura, ressentimento que fica após um conflito.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "How you ___ a hard message changes how the other person receives it."
items.why: To frame = enquadrar; a forma como você enquadra a mensagem muda como ela é recebida.

items.q: "A reflective question opens doors that a direct one closes." Reflective here means…
options: thoughtful and softly phrased, inviting the other to think
items.why: Reflective = reflexivo; uma pergunta pensada e suave que convida à reflexão em vez de acusar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando se media um conflito no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's talk through what happened before we decide anything." To talk through means to…
options: discuss something carefully from start to finish
items.why: Talk through = conversar sobre algo com calma, do início ao fim, para entender.

items.q: "I don't think anyone dropped the ball here." To drop the ball means to…
options: fail to do your part or make a careless mistake
items.why: Drop the ball = falhar na sua parte, deixar cair a bola.

items.q: "Before we fix anything, let's cool off for a moment." To cool off means to…
items.why: Cool off = se acalmar depois de ficar irritado.

items.q: "Once you both calm down, we can clear the air." To clear the air means to…
options: remove tension by talking openly about the problem
items.why: Clear the air = limpar o ar, resolver o mal-estar conversando abertamente.

items.q: "Let's walk through the timeline together, step by step." To walk through means to…
options: examine something in detail, one step at a time
items.why: Walk through = percorrer/revisar algo passo a passo em detalhe.
